headline: Treat each whole word as one token
statement: Return every starting index in s of a substring formed by concatenating each word in words exactly once, in any order. All words have the same nonzero length; duplicate words count separately. Return indices in any order.
constraints: All words have equal length between 1 and 30
s and words contain lowercase English letters
intuition: All the words have the same length, so read the string in whole-word chunks. Keep a moving group of chunks and count each word. Remove chunks from the left if a word appears too often. Try each possible starting alignment so no valid starting position is missed.
approach: Count required word occurrence counts and scan each offset modulo word length.
Add a word-sized token; clear the window if it is not required.
When a count exceeds its required count, remove left tokens until valid again.
Once the window contains exactly len(words) tokens, record its start.
correctness: Each aligned window contains only required words and no count above its required count. If its token count equals the total required count, every required count must be exactly satisfied. Shrinking removes only invalid starts; scanning all offsets includes every possible starting index.
bruteForce: For each start, slice and count all words in the candidate: O(n*m*w) work for n characters, m words and width w.

complexity.explanation: Time O(n*w + m*w); additional space O(m*w). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: Duplicate words need occurrence counts, not a set.
Scan every offset, including starts inside the first word width.
Shrink repeatedly on overflow; overlapping answers are allowed.
